cor-prc-bic.title: Where the BIC comes from
cor-prc-bic.html:
Under the conditions of @thm-prc-laplace, suppose in addition that Hn/n→H¯ positive definite, that the prior is continuous and positive at the limit of 𝛃β^n, and that 𝛃β^ maximizes ℓ with 𝛃𝛃ℓ(β^)−ℓ(β^n)=O(n−1). Then 𝛃−2log⁡m(y)=−2ℓ(β^)+plog⁡n+O(1),{#eq-prc-bic}

where the O(1) term is 𝛃log⁡det(Hn/n)−plog⁡(2π)−2log⁡π(β^n)+o(1). The leading two terms are the BIC of @def-sel-aic-bic.

def-prc-mcmc.title: Metropolis–Hastings, Gibbs, and the two diagnostics
def-prc-mcmc.title_html: Metropolis–Hastings, Gibbs, and the two diagnostics
def-prc-mcmc.html:
Let π(⋅∣y) be a density known up to a constant.

  1. The Metropolis–Hastings chain with proposal density q(⋅∣⋅) moves from 𝛃β(t) by drawing 𝛃𝛃β∗∼q(⋅∣β(t)) and setting 𝛃𝛃β(t+1)=β∗ with probability 𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃α(β∗∣β(t))=min{1, π(β∗∣y)q(β(t)∣β∗)π(β(t)∣y)q(β∗∣β(t))},{#eq-prc-mh}

    and 𝛃𝛃β(t+1)=β(t) otherwise. The normalizing constant cancels. A symmetric proposal, q(b∣b′)=q(b′∣b), gives the random-walk Metropolis algorithm, in which α is the ratio of posterior densities capped at one.

  2. The Gibbs sampler partitions 𝛙𝛙𝛙ψ=(ψ1,…,ψK) and replaces each block in turn by a draw from its full conditional 𝛙𝛙π(ψk∣ψ−k,y). It is the special case of (a) in which every proposal is accepted.

  3. For c chains of length N, split each in half and let W be the mean of the 2c within-sequence variances and B the variance of the 2c sequence means. The potential scale reduction is R^={(N/2−1)W/(N/2)+BW}1/2.{#eq-prc-rhat}

  4. With ρt the lag-t autocorrelation of the stationary chain, the effective sample size of cN draws is ESS=cN/(1+2∑t≥1ρt), the sum truncated by Geyer’s rule in the form used here: add the autocorrelations in consecutive pairs ρ2k−1+ρ2k, k=1,2,…, and stop at the first pair that is negative.

def-prc-posterior.title: The Bayesian generalized linear model
def-prc-posterior.html:
Let y follow the generalized linear model of @def-glm-model with link g, dispersion ϕ and log-likelihood 𝛃ℓ(β), and let π be a prior density on Rp. The posterior density of 𝛃β is 𝛃𝛃𝛃π(β∣y)=exp⁡{ℓ(β)}π(β)m(y),m(y)=∫Rpexp⁡{ℓ(b)}π(b)db,{#eq-prc-posterior}

whenever 0<m(y)<∞; the posterior is then proper. The maximum a posteriori estimate 𝛃β^MAP maximizes @eq-prc-posterior, equivalently maximizes the penalized log-likelihood 𝛃𝛃ℓ(β)+log⁡π(β). The default choice throughout this chapter is the independent normal prior 𝛃β∼Np(m,Σ), for which 𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃log⁡π(β∣y)=ℓ(β)−12(β−m)⊤Σ−1(β−m)+const.{#eq-prc-normal-prior-post}

def-prc-ppc.title: Posterior predictive distribution and check
def-prc-ppc.html:
The posterior predictive distribution of a replicate data set Yrep is 𝛃𝛃𝛃p(yrep∣y)=∫f(yrep∣β)π(β∣y)dβ,{#eq-prc-ppd}

which is sampled by drawing 𝛃β from the posterior and then yrep from the model. For a statistic T the posterior predictive p-value is Pr{T(Yrep)≥T(y)∣y}, or the lower-tail version Pr{T(Yrep)≤T(y)∣y} when small values of T are the departure of interest, estimated by the proportion of replicates on the relevant side of the observed value.

exm-prc-anes-mcmc.title: The 1996 survey, sampled
exm-prc-anes-mcmc.html:
Return to the logistic regression of @exm-bin-anes: the intended vote of 944 respondents on party identification, age in decades, education and income. Put an independent N(0,102) prior on each of the 5 coefficients — nearly flat on this scale — and run four random-walk Metropolis chains of 8000 draws from starts 8 posterior standard deviations away in every coordinate, with the Laplace covariance as the proposal shape and scale 2.38/5. The acceptance rate is 0.298, and discarding the first half of each chain leaves 16000 draws.

Panel (a) of Figure 39.4.2 shows the four chains for the party coefficient: two of them climb far above the mode before turning back, and all four are indistinguishable once the first few hundred iterations are past. Panel (b) applies the whole recipe — discard the first half, then split what is left — at each run length, and plots R^−1 on a log scale. It starts at 5.63 with 200 draws per chain, is below 1.05 by 1000 and below 1.02 by 1400, and its own Monte Carlo variability keeps it brushing the 1.01 line until about 6000; at the full eight thousand the largest value over the five coefficients is 1.0066. Effective sample size is the binding constraint: 1079, or 0.067 effective draws per iteration.

The posterior mean of that coefficient is 1.2300 with posterior standard deviation 0.0705, against the maximum likelihood 1.2188 and standard error 0.0709: with n=944 and a prior this weak the two analyses agree to the second decimal, as @thm-prc-laplace and the Bernstein–von Mises theorem say they must. What the simulation buys is the ability to ask for any posterior summary at all.

The probit version, sampled by @prp-prc-albert-chib with 4000 draws per chain, gives posterior mean 0.6780 against the maximum likelihood 0.6733; the ratio of the logistic coefficient to it is 1.814, against the π/3=1.8138 of @prp-bin-latent-scale. Its effective sample size per iteration is 0.092, half again as good and with no tuning, though each iteration costs n truncated normal draws. Panel (c) compares the two autocorrelation functions.

exm-prc-laplace.title: How good is the approximation
exm-prc-laplace.html:
Take a logistic regression with an intercept and one covariate, a N(0,52) prior on each coefficient, and data simulated at 𝛃β=(−0.4,1.2)⊤. Adaptive Gauss–Hermite quadrature on a tensor grid centred at the mode computes @eq-prc-posterior to machine accuracy, so the Laplace error can be measured exactly.

At n=25 the Laplace marginal likelihood is too small by 0.10700, or eleven per cent; the relative error falls to 0.001114 at n=1600. Regressing the log error on log⁡n over seven sample sizes gives a slope of −1.06, and over those seven sizes the product n×error stays between 1.530 and 2.675: the O(n−1) of @eq-prc-laplace, over a decade and a half of sample sizes (Figure 39.4.1, panel (b)).

Panel (a) shows what that error looks like at n=25: the marginal posterior of the slope is visibly right-skewed, mean 2.3291 against mode 1.9271, with total variation distance 0.1827 to the normal approximation. Reporting the mode with the curvature as a standard error would put the estimate in the wrong place and the interval on the wrong side. The corollary is visible too: over the same seven sizes the gap between the BIC and −2log⁡m(y) stays between −3.41 and −1.61, an O(1) that does not grow.

exm-prc-ppc.title: Where the survey model fails
exm-prc-ppc.html:
The model of @exm-prc-anes-mcmc treats party identification as a single linear term. Take T to be the number of Dole votes among the 108 respondents who called themselves independent Democrats — a subgroup the model has no parameter for. Observed: 7; across four thousand posterior predictive replicates the mean is 14.4, and only 0.034 of them are as low as seven (Figure 39.4.3, panel (a)). Given the conservatism just described, that is a real signal.

It is not one a quadratic term would catch: adding PID2 drops the deviance by 0.019, while treating party identification as a seven-level factor drops it by 12.68 on five degrees of freedom, p=0.027 — the same finding from the likelihood side. Panel (b) shows why: at average covariates the fitted curve passes well above the observed proportion at party identification two and below it at four. The monotone logistic curve is not flexible enough near the middle of this scale.

exm-prc-separated-bayes.title: The separated subgroup, three priors
exm-prc-separated-bayes.html:
@exm-bin-separated fitted the intended vote on party identification among the 13 respondents whose schooling stopped at or before the eighth grade, and found complete separation: no maximum likelihood estimate exists, and software reports whatever coefficient its iteration limit produced. With only two parameters the posterior can be computed by quadrature, under any prior at all — over the whole plane, by the substitution β=stan⁡u, since under separation a Cauchy posterior has a polynomial tail and any fixed box would discard a large part of it.

Under the flat prior the posterior is not a distribution at all, and the arithmetic shows it: integrating the likelihood over a square box centred at the origin gives 8.7 for half-width ten and 778.6 for half-width eighty, each doubling multiplying the mass by at least 4.13. That is the area of the separating cone growing, as in the proof of @prp-prc-propriety(b), and no amount of sampling will reveal it — a chain started near the data’s own scale looks well behaved while wandering up a ridge of infinite mass.

An independent N(0,2.52) prior on the slope and N(0,102) on the intercept gives a proper posterior with mean 3.077, median 2.931 and a central 95 per cent credible interval of (1.046, 5.922). Independent Cauchy priors of the same scales give mean 6.091, median 4.001 and interval (1.127, 22.995). Both exclude zero decisively. Both lower endpoints agree to within a tenth, and the upper endpoints differ by a factor of 3.9: the data bound the effect from below, and everything above that is prior. Panel (b) of Figure 39.5.1 shows the two posteriors.

Set these beside the frequentist answers of Section 35.3. The ordinary likelihood ratio gives the one-sided interval (0.902,∞): the most honest statement available without a prior, and the least useful. Firth’s penalty, the mode under the Jeffreys prior (@prp-bin-firth), gives 1.362 with the penalized likelihood ratio interval (0.364,4.045) — smaller than either posterior median, and a mode rather than a mean. The Jeffreys penalty falls off exponentially along the separating ray (@prp-bin-firth) while a Cauchy of scale 2.5 falls off only polynomially, so it bites hardest on exactly the direction the data do not constrain. There is no way to choose among these numbers from the data. Thirteen observations that separate perfectly contain a bound and nothing more, and every method reports that bound plus whatever it assumed. The discipline is to say which assumption produced which number, and to notice that the flat prior is not the assumption-free option but the one whose assumption is inconsistent.

exm-prc-strikes.title: How long does a strike last
exm-prc-strikes.title_html: How long does a strike last
exm-prc-strikes.html:
The durations of 62 contract strikes in United States manufacturing, from one day to 216, are recorded with a measure of unanticipated industrial production at the time. @exm-ql-strikes-fit read the same durations as counts and asked only for a variance function; here they are read as what they are, positive and continuous, and the question is which family to use. The response is strongly right-skewed, so a normal linear model is out; which of the positive families fits the mean–variance relationship?

The covariate takes only 9 distinct values, so the data arrive already in replicate groups, of sizes 2 to 18. The weighted regression of @prp-prc-model-building(a) gives ζ^=1.606 with a standard error of 0.434, computed from the exact normal-theory variance Var(log⁡sg2)=ψ′{(mg−1)/2} — the familiar 2/(mg−1) is only its large-group limit, and understates it badly for the two groups of size two. Panel (a) of Figure 39.1.1 shows the nine points with the fitted line and the Poisson and gamma references: ζ=2 is 0.9 standard errors away and ζ=1 is 1.4, which is weak evidence for the gamma and against anything Poisson-like.

Fit three models with a log link and the same linear predictor, maximizing each over its dispersion parameter as well as over 𝛃β, and count d=3 for all three. AIC on the scale of the durations is 585.4 for the gamma, 590.9 for the log-normal and 603.3 for the inverse Gaussian. The log-normal figure is the AIC of the least squares fit to log⁡y, 206.8, plus the Jacobian term 2∑ilog⁡yi=384.1 of @eq-prc-jacobian. Without that term the log-normal appears to beat the gamma by 378.7: not a close call, and in the wrong direction, because the uncorrected number answers a different question. Leave-one-out cross-validation with the log score puts the three in the same order, at −4.7192, −4.7713 and −4.8664 per observation.

The gamma slope is to the last decimal the estimate that @exm-ql-strikes-fit obtained from V(μ)=μ2 alone: the variance function fixes the estimating equations, and choosing a family on top of it buys a likelihood, not a different fit. The maximum likelihood shape of the gamma fit is ν^=1.003, so the durations are close to exponential given the covariate, which is what ζ=2 with a coefficient of variation near one means. (Software reports instead the moment estimate from the Pearson dispersion ϕ^=0.941, namely 1.063; the two agree here, and for the inverse Gaussian they do not.) The fits also disagree about what they estimate: at the mean covariate value the gamma model puts the mean duration at 39.4 days, while the log-normal model puts the median at 22.2 and, after the retransformation correction of @prp-tr-retransformation, the mean at 46.7.

exm-prc-tvnews.title: Days of television news
exm-prc-tvnews.html:
The 1996 American National Election Studies survey asked its 944 respondents on how many of the past seven days they had watched the television news. Treating the answer as a binomial count out of seven and fitting a logit model in age, education and income gives a deviance of 4447.3 on 940 degrees of freedom and a Pearson statistic of 3598.2, so ϕ^=3.828: the model is not close to fitting.

Panel (a) of Figure 39.2.1 is the half-normal plot with an envelope from B=19 simulated data sets, refitted each time. Every one of the 944 ordered residuals lies above the band — not a little too large in the tail but too large everywhere, the signature of a dispersion problem rather than of outliers.

The targeted checks of @prp-prc-diagnostics say where the trouble is not. Adding η^2 drops the deviance by 0.31 on one degree of freedom, p=0.580: the logit link is not the problem. Adding a quadratic in age drops it by 0.03, and panel (a) of Figure 39.2.2 shows the partial residual for age with a smooth that is mildly concave but close to the fitted line, so the scale of age is not the problem either. The leverages are all tiny — the largest 0.0144 against an average of 0.0042 — and the largest Cook-type distance is 0.0970.

What is left is the variance function, and panel (b) makes the case. The local means of |rP| in ten equal bins of the linear predictor run from 1.25 to 1.91, against a reference height of 2/π≈0.80, and they drift upward: the regression of log⁡(rP)2 on the linear predictor has slope 0.381 with t=4.21, so the excess variance is not even constant. The binomial model treats a respondent’s seven days as seven independent trials with a common probability, and they are nothing of the kind: 161 respondents watched on none of the seven days and 288 on all seven. Habits are not coin flips.

The repair is a variance function with a second parameter. A beta-binomial model, in which each respondent has a latent probability from a beta distribution with mean πi and precision s, gives s^=1.072, a within-respondent correlation of ρ=1/(1+s)=0.483, and the variance 7πi(1−πi)(7+s)/(1+s), about 3.90 times the binomial one, against the ϕ^=3.828 estimated directly. Panel (b) of Figure 39.2.1 repeats the half-normal plot under that model: only 0.2 per cent of the ordered residuals now lie above the envelope, although 22.8 per cent still fall below it, against a pointwise level of 5 per cent on that side — a residual misfit at the bottom of the scale that the beta-binomial does not remove.

The consequences for inference are what Chapter 38 predicts. The age coefficient barely moves, from 0.0424 to 0.0405; its standard error moves from 0.0018 to 0.0033, and the quasi-binomial standard error — the binomial one multiplied by ϕ^ — is 0.0034, which agrees with the beta-binomial one to two figures. The education coefficient is the casualty: 0.0233 with standard error 0.0178 under the binomial, already unconvincing at t=1.3, becomes −0.0013 with standard error 0.0343 — an effect of zero with three times the uncertainty.

exr-prc-additivity-three.title: C1
exr-prc-additivity-three.html: Extend @prp-prc-model-building(b) to three covariates: if g(μ)=a1(x1)+a2(x2)+a3(x3) with all three nonconstant and continuous, and g~(μ) is also a sum of three functions of the separate covariates, must s=g~∘g−1 be affine? Does the conclusion change if only two of the three are required to separate?

exr-prc-betabinom-variance.title: B2
exr-prc-betabinom-variance.html: Let Y∣Π∼Binomial(m,Π) with Π∼Beta(sπ,s(1−π)). Show that E(Y)=mπ and Var(Y)=mπ(1−π)(m+s)/(1+s), and that the ratio to the binomial variance is 1+(m−1)ρ with ρ=1/(1+s). Evaluate at m=7 and the fitted s^=1.072.

exr-prc-bic-prior.title: B2
exr-prc-bic-prior.html: @cor-prc-bic says the prior enters only the O(1) remainder. Show that if the prior is itself allowed to depend on n — say 𝛃β∼Np(0,nΣ0) with Σ0 fixed, so that the prior is made vaguer as data accumulate — then the remainder grows like plog⁡n, and say what that does to the BIC.

exr-prc-bimodal-probit.title: C1
exr-prc-bimodal-probit.html: Redo @prp-prc-priors(c) for the probit link: with η∼N(0,σ2) and π=Φ(η), show that the induced density of π is unimodal when σ2≤1 and bimodal when σ2>1, and say why the threshold differs from the logit’s.

exr-prc-cauchy-mixture.title: B1
exr-prc-cauchy-mixture.html: Show that a Cauchy prior with scale s is a scale mixture of normals: γ∣λ∼N(0,λ) with λ having an inverse gamma distribution with shape 1/2 and rate s2/2. Explain how this turns a Cauchy prior into a Gibbs sampler with normal full conditionals in the probit model.

exr-prc-credible-invariance.title: A2
exr-prc-credible-invariance.html: An equal-tailed credible interval for βj transforms to an equal-tailed credible interval for eβj by exponentiating its endpoints. Is the same true of a highest-posterior-density interval? Explain.

exr-prc-dy-prior.title: B1
exr-prc-dy-prior.html: Take the Poisson family with a log link, p=1 and xi1=1 for all i, so the model has a single parameter β and μ=eβ. Write out @eq-prc-dy explicitly, show that it is the density of β=log⁡μ when μ has a gamma distribution, and identify the shape and rate in terms of m0 and the vi. Why does the closed form appear here and not in general?

exr-prc-envelope-level.title: A1
exr-prc-envelope-level.html: @prp-prc-diagnostics(b) gives the pointwise level 2/(B+1). What is B for a level of 5 per cent? If instead the envelope is taken to be the second smallest and second largest of B simulated values, what is the pointwise level?

exr-prc-ess-thinning.title: B3
exr-prc-ess-thinning.html: A chain of 16000 draws has effective sample size 1000. A colleague thins it by keeping every sixteenth draw, obtaining 1000 nearly independent draws, and says nothing has been lost. Is that right? What is thinning good for?

exr-prc-firth-jeffreys.title: B3
exr-prc-firth-jeffreys.html: @prp-bin-firth adds 12log⁡det(X⊤WX) to the log-likelihood. Show that this is the log of the Jeffreys prior density for the logistic model, so Firth’s estimate is a posterior mode. Why does that mode exist even under separation, when the maximum likelihood estimate does not?

exr-prc-gamma-canonical.title: B1
exr-prc-gamma-canonical.html: The canonical link of the gamma family is g(μ)=−1/μ (@exm-glm-gamma). Show that with this link and a model matrix containing an intercept, the parameter space 𝛃𝛃{β:x(i)⊤β<0 for all i} is an open convex cone, and that the maximum likelihood estimate may fail to exist by running to its boundary. Contrast with the log link.

exr-prc-gibbs-as-mh.title: C1
exr-prc-gibbs-as-mh.html: Show that the Gibbs update of a block 𝛙ψk is a Metropolis–Hastings step with proposal 𝛙𝛙𝛙𝛙q(ψ∗∣ψ)=π(ψk∗∣ψ−k,y) and that its acceptance probability is one. Deduce that @prp-prc-mh-invariance covers the Gibbs sampler, and explain why a Gibbs sampler can nevertheless fail to be irreducible.

exr-prc-interaction-scale.title: A2
exr-prc-interaction-scale.html: A two-by-two table of counts has fitted means μ11=10, μ12=20, μ21=15 and μ22=30. Is there an interaction on the log scale? On the identity scale? Reconcile the two answers with @prp-prc-model-building(b).

exr-prc-laplace-onedim.title: B1
exr-prc-laplace-onedim.html: Take qn(β)=ng(β) for a fixed smooth g with a unique interior maximum at β∗ and g″(β∗)<0, and suppose g is bounded away from its maximum outside any neighbourhood of β∗. Verify (L1)–(L3) of @thm-prc-laplace and write out the approximation explicitly.

exr-prc-link-test-reading.title: A2
exr-prc-link-test-reading.html: The link test of @prp-prc-diagnostics(d) came out non-significant in @exm-prc-tvnews. Is that evidence that the logit link is correct? What would a significant result have shown?

exr-prc-logscore-deviance.title: B2
exr-prc-logscore-deviance.html: Show that for a family with ϕ=1 the leave-one-out log score and the leave-one-out deviance differ by a constant that does not depend on the model, so the two rank models identically. Show that this fails when ϕ is estimated.

exr-prc-mh-symmetric.title: A1
exr-prc-mh-symmetric.html: Show that for a symmetric proposal the acceptance probability @eq-prc-mh reduces to 𝛃𝛃min{1,exp⁡(qn(β∗)−qn(β(t)))}, and that an uphill move is always accepted.

exr-prc-power-link.title: C2
exr-prc-power-link.html: Let the true link belong to the power family gλ(μ)=(μλ−1)/λ, which has g0=log, and let the model actually fitted use the log link. Following the constructed-variable argument of @prp-tr-constructed, expand gλ about λ=0 to show that a one degree of freedom test of λ=0 is obtained by adding a multiple of η^2 to the linear predictor, and identify the constructed variable and the multiple exactly.

exr-prc-prior-probability.title: B2
exr-prc-prior-probability.html: For σ=10, compute the prior probability that π=eη/(1+eη)<0.01 when η∼N(0,σ2), and compare with σ=1. Relate the answers to @prp-prc-priors(c).

exr-prc-quadratic-check.title: A1
exr-prc-quadratic-check.html: Verify directly, from the form of the Poisson log-likelihood with a log link, that it is not a quadratic in 𝛃β for p=1, and identify the term that spoils it.

exr-prc-quadratic-noncanonical.title: C1
exr-prc-quadratic-noncanonical.html: @prp-prc-quadratic assumed the canonical link. Show that with a non-canonical link the conclusion still holds in the following sense: if the log-likelihood is a quadratic in 𝛃β for every design and every response, then the working weights of @thm-glm-irls do not depend on 𝛃β and the mean is affine in 𝛃β. Deduce that the model is the normal linear model up to a reparameterization.

exr-prc-rhat-reading.title: A2
exr-prc-rhat-reading.html: A chain is run once, from a start far from the posterior mode, and R^ computed from its two halves is 1.00. Is that evidence of convergence? What does the definition in @eq-prc-rhat require?

exr-prc-scale-aic.title: A1
exr-prc-scale-aic.html: A colleague fits a normal linear model to y and a Poisson log-linear model to y, and compares the two AIC values printed by the software. What is the correction term of @prp-prc-model-building(c) here, and in which direction does omitting it push the comparison?

exr-prc-sigma-two.title: A2
exr-prc-sigma-two.html: Explain in words why the induced prior of @prp-prc-priors(c) becomes U-shaped for large σ, without using the calculus of the proof.

exr-prc-simultaneous-envelope.title: C1
exr-prc-simultaneous-envelope.html: @prp-prc-diagnostics(b) says the simultaneous level of an envelope exceeds the pointwise one. Construct a simultaneous band from the same B simulations, by computing for each simulated data set the maximum over k of the standardized deviation {Rk(b)−R¯k}/sdk and using its (1−α) quantile. Show that the resulting band has simultaneous level at most α under the same exchangeability assumption, and say what it costs.

exr-prc-standardized.title: B1
exr-prc-standardized.html: Show that in a normal linear model with ϕ=σ2 and the identity link, @prp-prc-diagnostics(a) reduces to the exact statement 𝛆Cov(ε^)=σ2(I−M) of @eq-res-residual-moments, and that the standardization by 1−hii is then exact rather than approximate.

exr-prc-tau-lambda.title: A1
exr-prc-tau-lambda.html: A colleague reports a ridge-penalized logistic fit with λ=100 on standardized covariates. What normal prior does that correspond to, and what odds ratio for a one standard deviation change does the prior regard as, say, two standard deviations from zero?

prp-prc-albert-chib.title: The Albert–Chib sampler
prp-prc-albert-chib.html:
Consider the ungrouped probit model 𝛃Pr(Yi=1)=Φ(x(i)⊤β) with prior 𝛃β∼Np(m,Σ). Introduce latent variables 𝛃𝛃Zi∣β∼N(x(i)⊤β,1), independent, and set Yi=1{Zi>0}. Then:

  1. the marginal distribution of Y given 𝛃β is the probit model, so the posterior of 𝛃β is unchanged;

  2. given z and y, 𝛃β∼Np(V(X⊤z+Σ−1m),V) with V=(X⊤X+Σ−1)−1;

  3. given 𝛃β and y, the Zi are independent, Zi being 𝛃N(x(i)⊤β,1) truncated to (0,∞) if yi=1 and to (−∞,0) if yi=0.

prp-prc-diagnostics.title: What the standard diagnostics measure
prp-prc-diagnostics.html:
Let a generalized linear model be fitted by maximum likelihood, let W^=diag{wih′(η^i)2/V(μ^i)} be the working weights, H=W^1/2X(X⊤W^X)−1X⊤W^1/2 the weighted hat matrix and hii its diagonal.

  1. (Moments of the Pearson residuals.) To first order in the expansion behind @thm-glm-asymptotics, E(riP)≈0 and Var(riP)≈1−hii, and the standardized residual riP/1−hii has approximate variance one. Moreover ∑ihii=p, so hii averages p/n.

  2. (Level of a simulated envelope.) Let |r|(1)≤⋯≤|r|(n) be the ordered absolute residuals, and let B independent data sets be generated from the fitted model and refitted, giving vectors of ordered absolute residuals whose kth entries are Rk(1),…,Rk(B). If the model is correct and the fitted parameters are the true ones, and the B+1 values |r|(k),Rk(1),…,Rk(B) are exchangeable with no ties, then Pr{|r|(k)<minbRk(b) or |r|(k)>maxbRk(b)}=2B+1{#eq-prc-envelope}

    for each fixed k. The probability that some k leaves the band is larger than 2/(B+1), and no better than the union bound min{1,2n/(B+1)} without further argument.

  3. (Influence.) The one-step deletion results of @thm-res-deletion hold with X replaced by W^1/2X and y by the working response z of @eq-glm-working-response, giving the Cook-type measure Ci=(riP)2hii/{p(1−hii)2} of @def-res-cooks. The exact deletion identities do not hold, because removing a case changes the weights as well.

  4. (Checking the link.) Let η^i be the fitted linear predictor and refit the model with η^i2 added as a covariate. Under the fitted link the extra coefficient is zero, so the deviance drop is asymptotically χ2(1); a significant drop says the link is wrong, not which link is right.

  5. (Checking a covariate: two plots.) The partial residual for covariate j on the link scale is uij=β^jxij+(yi−μ^i)/h′(η^i). Its weighted least squares regression on [1,xj] with weights W^ has slope β^j exactly, so a smooth of uij against xij that departs from a straight line indicates a wrong scale for xj, as in @prp-res-partial-residual. The added-variable plot is the other half of the pair: let z~ and x~j be the residuals of the working response z and of xj after W^-weighted regression on the remaining columns X−j. Then the W^-weighted regression of z~ on x~j has slope exactly β^j, so curvature or a single dominating point in that plot is a statement about β^j itself.

  6. (Checking the variance function.) If the assumed variance function is correct then E|riP|≈2/π for every i, so a plot of |riP| against η^i should be level. A systematic trend indicates a variance function of the wrong shape; a level plot at the wrong height indicates a dispersion ϕ≠1.

prp-prc-mh-invariance.title: The chain has the right stationary distribution
prp-prc-mh-invariance.title_html: The chain has the right stationary distribution
prp-prc-mh-invariance.html: Let π be a density on Rp and q(⋅∣⋅) a transition density with q(b′∣b)>0 whenever q(b∣b′)>0. The Metropolis–Hastings kernel of @eq-prc-mh satisfies detailed balance with respect to π: π(b)q(b′∣b)α(b′∣b)=π(b′)q(b∣b′)α(b∣b′)for all b≠b′, and consequently π is a stationary distribution of the chain.

prp-prc-model-building.title: Three facts about building a generalized linear model
prp-prc-model-building.title_html: Three facts about building a generalized linear model
prp-prc-model-building.html:
1. (Reading the variance function off replicates.) Suppose the observations fall into G≥2 groups, group g holding mg≥2 independent replicates with mean μg>0, variance ϕμgζ and finite fourth moment. Let y¯g be the mean of the replicates in group g, let sg2 be their variance with divisor mg−1, and let ζ^ be the slope of the weighted least squares regression of log⁡sg2 on log⁡y¯g with any fixed positive weights cg. If the log⁡μg are not all equal, then ζ^→ζ in probability as mingmg→∞ with G, the μg and ϕ fixed.

  2. (Additivity is a property of the link, not of the data.) Let g(μ(x1,x2))=a(x1)+b(x2) on I1×I2, with a and b continuous and nonconstant, and let J be the interval of values taken by a+b. Let g~ be a second link and s=g~∘g−1, twice differentiable on J. Then g~(μ(x1,x2)) is again a sum of a function of x1 and a function of x2 if and only if s is affine on J.

  3. (Comparing models across response scales.) Let t be strictly increasing and continuously differentiable with t′>0, and let a model for the transformed responses y~i=t(yi) have maximized log-likelihood ℓ~ and d estimated parameters. As a model for y it has maximized log-likelihood ℓ~+∑ilog⁡t′(yi), so its AIC on the scale of y is AIC=−2ℓ~+2d−2∑i=1nlog⁡t′(yi).{#eq-prc-jacobian}

prp-prc-priors.title: What a prior does
prp-prc-priors.html:
Let ℓ be the log-likelihood of a generalized linear model with rank(X)=p and a concave log-likelihood (@thm-glm-concave), and write 𝛃𝛄β=(β0,γ⊤)⊤ with β0 an intercept.

  1. (Normal prior, ridge penalty.) Under γj∼N(0,τ2) independently and a flat prior on β0, the posterior mode maximizes 𝛃𝛄ℓ(β)−12λ‖γ‖2 with λ=1/τ2. If ℓ is bounded above, as it is for the binomial and the Poisson, and the response is not constant — for the binomial, both outcomes occur — the mode exists and is unique whether or not the data are separated. The hypothesis on the response cannot be dropped: with a flat prior on β0 the objective is not coercive in β0 when every yi is 1. Penalizing the intercept as well makes existence unconditional.

  2. (Laplace prior, lasso penalty.) Under γj independent with density (2b)−1e−|γj|/b and a flat prior on β0, the posterior mode maximizes 𝛃ℓ(β)−λ∑j|γj| with λ=1/b, and is therefore the lasso-penalized estimate of @def-shr-lasso, with exact zeros. The posterior, by contrast, is never sparse: whenever it is proper, Pr(γj=0∣y)=0 for every j.

  3. (What a normal prior says about a probability.) In a binary model with logit link, suppose the linear predictor at some covariate value has the prior η∼N(0,σ2). The induced prior density of π=eη/(1+eη) on (0,1) is unimodal with mode 1/2 if σ2≤2, and has exactly two modes, symmetric about 1/2, with a local minimum at 1/2, if σ2>2.

  4. (Existence.) Under the prior of (a), or under independent Cauchy priors on the γj with a flat prior on β0, the logistic posterior mode exists for every data set in which both outcomes occur, separated or not; under (a) it is also unique. Under any proper prior the posterior itself is proper (@prp-prc-propriety(a)), so posterior means and credible intervals exist whether or not the maximum likelihood estimate does.

prp-prc-propriety.title: When a flat prior gives a posterior
prp-prc-propriety.title_html: When a flat prior gives a posterior
prp-prc-propriety.html:
Let π be a prior on Rp.

  1. If π is proper and the likelihood is bounded, the posterior is proper. Both the logistic and the Poisson likelihoods are bounded.

  2. Take the improper prior π∝1 and the ungrouped logistic model with rank(X)=p. Then the posterior is proper if and only if the data are in overlap in the sense of @def-bin-separation, that is if and only if the maximum likelihood estimate exists (@thm-bin-separation).

prp-prc-quadratic.title: Why the conjugate machinery stops at the normal family
prp-prc-quadratic.title_html: Why the conjugate machinery stops at the normal family
prp-prc-quadratic.html:
Let y follow the exponential dispersion family of @def-glm-model with the canonical link, so that 𝛃θi=x(i)⊤β and 𝛃ℓ(β)=ϕ−1∑iwi{yiθi−b(θi)}+c. Suppose b is twice continuously differentiable on an open interval Θ. Then the following are equivalent.

  1. For every n, every X with rank(X)=p and every y, the function 𝛃𝛃β↦ℓ(β) is a quadratic polynomial on 𝛃𝛃{β:x(i)⊤β∈Θ}.

  2. b″ is constant on Θ.

  3. The variance function is constant: V(μ)=b″(θ) does not depend on μ, so the family is normal (@exr-glm-variance-determines).

Consequently, for every family except the normal, a normal prior on 𝛃β gives a posterior that is not normal and has no closed-form normalizing constant.

thm-prc-laplace.title: Laplace approximation
thm-prc-laplace.html:
Let ρn=n−3/8 and 𝛃𝛃𝛃Bn={β:‖β−β^n‖≤ρn}, and suppose there are constants 0<c≤C<∞ and a,K>0, free of n, with:

  1. qn is four times continuously differentiable on Bn, with 𝛃∇qn(β^n)=0 and Hn positive definite;

  2. cn≤λmin(Hn)≤λmax(Hn)≤Cn, and every third and fourth partial derivative of qn is bounded in absolute value by Cn on Bn;

  3. 𝛃𝛃𝛃∫Rp∖Bnexp⁡{qn(β)−qn(β^n)}dβ≤Kexp⁡(−an1/4).

Then 𝛃𝛃𝛃∫Rpeqn(β)dβ=(2π)p/2det(Hn)−1/2eqn(β^n){1+O(n−1)}.{#eq-prc-laplace}
